title: 2013 HMMT February Guts Problem 1
statement: Arpon chooses a positive real number \(k\). For each positive integer \(n\), he places a marker at the point \((n, n k)\) in the \((x, y)\) plane. Suppose that two markers whose \(x\) coordinates differ by 4 have distance 31. What is the distance between the markers at \((7,7 k)\) and \((19,19 k)\) ?

solutions.text: 93 The difference of the \(x\)-coordinates of the markers is \(12=3 \cdot 4\). Thus, by similar triangles (where we draw right triangles whose legs are parallel to the axes and whose hypotenuses lie along the line \(y=k x\) ), the distance between the markers is \(3 \cdot 31=93\).
